import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_2.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_31_0: ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_31_1: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_31_2: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_31_0 and Source3_31_2 on 'movie_id'
# We join df0 and df2 on 'movie_id' to bring movie titles to the ratings
df_joined = pd.merge(df2, df0[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Operation 2: JOIN the above result with Source3_31_1 on 'user_id' to get gender info
df_joined = pd.merge(df_joined, df1[['user_id', 'gender']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Operation 3: PIVOT with group_by = [title], aggregations = 
# avg(rating) grouped by gender F and avg(rating) grouped by gender M

# Group by title and gender, calculate average rating
grouped = df_joined.groupby(['title', 'gender'], as_index=False)['rating'].mean()

# Pivot so that genders become columns 'F' and 'M'
pivot = grouped.pivot(index='title', columns='gender', values='rating')

# Rename columns to match target schema ['title', 'F', 'M']
pivot = pivot.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'}).reset_index()

# Ensure columns order and types
pivot = pivot[['title', 'F', 'M']]

# Convert 'F' and 'M' columns to float explicitly (they should already be float)
pivot['F'] = pivot['F'].astype(float)
pivot['M'] = pivot['M'].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/target_multisource.csv"
pivot.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_31_2 and Source3_31_1 on user_id to get gender info for each rating
joined_user_rating = pd.merge(source2, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_31_0 on movie_id to get movie titles
joined_all = pd.merge(joined_user_rating, source0, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Pivot table to get average rating by gender per title
pivot = joined_all.pivot_table(
    index="title",
    columns="gender",
    values="rating",
    aggfunc="mean"
).reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
pivot = pivot.rename(columns={"F": "F", "M": "M"})

# Ensure columns order as in target schema
pivot = pivot[["title", "F", "M"]]

# Write output to the target file
pivot.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
